title: अंश १ · अध्याय १७

items.speaker: पाराशर उवाच
items.text:
मैत्रेय श्वूयतां सम्यक् चरितं तस्य धीमतः ।
प्रह्लादस्य सदोदारचीरितस्य महात्मनः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
maitreya śvūyatāṃ samyak caritaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ |
prahlādasya sadodāracīritasya mahātmanaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
दितेः पुत्रो महावीर्य्यो हिरण्यकशिपुः पुरा ।
त्रैलोक्यं वशमानिन्ये ब्रह्मणो वरदर्पितः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
diteḥ putro mahāvīryyo hiraṇyakaśipuḥ purā |
trailokyaṃ vaśamāninye brahmaṇo varadarpitaḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
इन्दत्वमकरोदू दैत्यः स चासीत् सविता स्वयम् ।
वायुरग्रिरपां नाथः सोमस्चाभूनूमहासुरः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
indatvamakarodū daityaḥ sa cāsīt savitā svayam |
vāyuragrirapāṃ nāthaḥ somascābhūnūmahāsuraḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
धनानामधिपः सोऽभूत् स एवासीत् खयं यमः ।
यज्ञभागानशेषांस्तु स स्वयं बुभुजेऽसुरः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
dhanānāmadhipaḥ so'bhūt sa evāsīt khayaṃ yamaḥ |
yajñabhāgānaśeṣāṃstu sa svayaṃ bubhuje'suraḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
देवाः सर्गं परित्यज्य ततूत्रासान्मुनिसत्तम ।
विचेरुरवनौ सर्वं बिब्राणा मानुषीं तनुम् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
devāḥ sargaṃ parityajya tatūtrāsānmunisattama |
viceruravanau sarvaṃ bibrāṇā mānuṣīṃ tanum || 5 ||

items.text:
जिताव त्रिभुव्रनं सर्व्वं त्रैलोक्यैश्वर्य्यदर्पितः ।
उपगीयामानो गन्धर्वैर्बुभुजे विषयान् प्रियान् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
jitāva tribhuvranaṃ sarvvaṃ trailokyaiśvaryyadarpitaḥ |
upagīyāmāno gandharvairbubhuje viṣayān priyān || 6 ||

items.text:
पानासक्तं महात्मानं हिरणंयकशिपु तदा ।
उपासाञ्चकिरे सर्व्वै सिद्धगन्धर्वपन्नगाः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
pānāsaktaṃ mahātmānaṃ hiraṇaṃyakaśipu tadā |
upāsāñcakire sarvvai siddhagandharvapannagāḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
अवादयञ्जगुश्चान्ये जयशब्दानथापरे ।
दैत्यराजस्य पुरतश्चक्रुः सिद्धा मुदन्विताः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
avādayañjaguścānye jayaśabdānathāpare |
daityarājasya purataścakruḥ siddhā mudanvitāḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
तत्र प्रनृत्याप्सरसि स्फटिकाभ्रमयेऽमुरः ।
पपौ पानं मुदा युक्तः प्रासादे सुमनोहरे ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
tatra pranṛtyāpsarasi sphaṭikābhramaye'muraḥ |
papau pānaṃ mudā yuktaḥ prāsāde sumanohare || 9 ||

items.text:
तस्य पुत्रो महाभागः प्रह्लादो नाम नामतः ।
पपाठ बालपाठयानि गुरुगेहे गतोऽर्भकः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tasya putro mahābhāgaḥ prahlādo nāma nāmataḥ |
papāṭha bālapāṭhayāni gurugehe gato'rbhakaḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
एकदा तुस धर्म्मात्मा जगाम गुरुणा सह ।
पानासक्तस्य पुरतः पितुर्दैत्यपतेस्तदा ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
ekadā tusa dharmmātmā jagāma guruṇā saha |
pānāsaktasya purataḥ piturdaityapatestadā || 11 ||

items.text:
पादप्रणामावनतं तमुत्थाप्य पिता सुतम् ।
हिरण्यकशिपुः प्राह प्रह्लादममितोजसम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
pādapraṇāmāvanataṃ tamutthāpya pitā sutam |
hiraṇyakaśipuḥ prāha prahlādamamitojasam || 12 ||

items.text:
पठयतां भवता वत्स ! सारभूतं सुभाषितम् ।
कालेनैतावता यत् ते सदोद्यु क्तने शिक्षितम् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
paṭhayatāṃ bhavatā vatsa ! sārabhūtaṃ subhāṣitam |
kālenaitāvatā yat te sadodyu ktane śikṣitam || 13 ||

items.text:
श्वूयतां तात ! वक्ष्यामि सारभूतं तवाज्ञया ।
समाहितमना भूत्वा यन्मे चेतस्यवस्थितम् ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
śvūyatāṃ tāta ! vakṣyāmi sārabhūtaṃ tavājñayā |
samāhitamanā bhūtvā yanme cetasyavasthitam || 14 ||

items.text:
अनादिमध्यान्तमजमवृद्धिक्षयमच्युतम् ।
प्रणातोऽस्मि महात्मानं सर्व्वकारणकारणम् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
anādimadhyāntamajamavṛddhikṣayamacyutam |
praṇāto'smi mahātmānaṃ sarvvakāraṇakāraṇam || 15 ||

items.text:
एवं निशम्य दैन्येन्द्रः क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ।
विलोक्य तदूगुरुं प्राह स्फुरिताधरपल्लवः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ niśamya dainyendraḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ |
vilokya tadūguruṃ prāha sphuritādharapallavaḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
ब्रह्मबन्धो ! किमेतत् ते विपक्षस्तुतिसहितम् ।
असारं ग्राहितो बालो मामवज्ञाय दुर्मते ! ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
brahmabandho ! kimetat te vipakṣastutisahitam |
asāraṃ grāhito bālo māmavajñāya durmate ! || 17 ||

items.text:
दैत्येश्वर ! न कोपस्य वशमागन्तुमर्हसि ।
ममोपदेशजनितं नायं वदति ते सुतः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
daityeśvara ! na kopasya vaśamāgantumarhasi |
mamopadeśajanitaṃ nāyaṃ vadati te sutaḥ || 18 ||

items.text:
अनुशास्तोसि केनेदृगु वत्स ! प्रह्लाद कथ्यताम् ।
ममोपदिष्ट नेत्येष प्रब्रवीति गुरुस्तव ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
anuśāstosi kenedṛgu vatsa ! prahlāda kathyatām |
mamopadiṣṭa netyeṣa prabravīti gurustava || 19 ||

items.text:
शास्ता विष्णुरशेषस्य जगतो यो ह्टदि स्थितः ।
तमृते परमात्मानं तात ! कः केन शास्यते ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
śāstā viṣṇuraśeṣasya jagato yo hṭadi sthitaḥ |
tamṛte paramātmānaṃ tāta ! kaḥ kena śāsyate || 20 ||

items.text:
कोऽय विष्णुः सुदुर्बुद्ध ! यं ब्रवीषि पुनः पुनः ।
जगतामीश्वरस्येह पुरतः प्रसभं मम ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
ko'ya viṣṇuḥ sudurbuddha ! yaṃ bravīṣi punaḥ punaḥ |
jagatāmīśvarasyeha purataḥ prasabhaṃ mama || 21 ||

items.text:
न शह्दगोचरे यस्य योगिध्येयं परं पदम् ।
यतो यश्व स्वयं विश्वं स विष्णुः परमेश्वरः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
na śahdagocare yasya yogidhyeyaṃ paraṃ padam |
yato yaśva svayaṃ viśvaṃ sa viṣṇuḥ parameśvaraḥ || 22 ||

items.text:
परमेश्वरसंज्ञोऽज्ञ ! किमन्यो मययवस्थिते ।
तवास्ति मर्त्तुकामस्त्व प्रब्रवीषि पुनः पुनः ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
parameśvarasaṃjño'jña ! kimanyo mayayavasthite |
tavāsti marttukāmastva prabravīṣi punaḥ punaḥ || 23 ||

items.text:
न केवलं तात ! मम प्रजानां स ब्रह्मभूतो भवतश्व विष्णुः ।
धाता विधाता परमेश्वरश्च प्रसीद कोपं कुरुषे किमर्थम ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
na kevalaṃ tāta ! mama prajānāṃ sa brahmabhūto bhavataśva viṣṇuḥ |
dhātā vidhātā parameśvaraśca prasīda kopaṃ kuruṣe kimarthama || 24 ||

items.text:
प्रविचष्टः कोऽस्य ह्टदये दुर्बुद्धेरतिपापकृत् ।
येनेदृशान्यसाधूनि वदत्याविष्टमानसः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
pravicaṣṭaḥ ko'sya hṭadaye durbuddheratipāpakṛt |
yenedṛśānyasādhūni vadatyāviṣṭamānasaḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
न केवलं मदूह्टदयं स विष्णु--राक्रम्य लोकान् सकलानवस्थितः ।
स मां त्वदादींश्च पितः ! समस्तान् समस्तचेष्टासु युनक्ति सर्वगः ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
na kevalaṃ madūhṭadayaṃ sa viṣṇu--rākramya lokān sakalānavasthitaḥ |
sa māṃ tvadādīṃśca pitaḥ ! samastān samastaceṣṭāsu yunakti sarvagaḥ || 26 ||

items.text:
निष्काम्यतामयं दुष्टः शास्यताञ्च गुरोगृ हे ।
योजितो दुर्म्मतिः केन विपक्षवितथस्तुतौ ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
niṣkāmyatāmayaṃ duṣṭaḥ śāsyatāñca gurogṛ he |
yojito durmmatiḥ kena vipakṣavitathastutau || 27 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्तोऽसौ तदा दैत्यैर्नीतो गुरुगृहं पुनः ।
जग्राह विद्यामनिशं गुरुशुश्वू षणोद्यतः ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
ityukto'sau tadā daityairnīto gurugṛhaṃ punaḥ |
jagrāha vidyāmaniśaṃ guruśuśvū ṣaṇodyataḥ || 28 ||

items.text:
कालेऽतीते च महति प्रह्लादमसुरेश्वरः ।
समाहूयाब्रवीत् पुत्र ! गाध काचित् प्रगीयताम् ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
kāle'tīte ca mahati prahlādamasureśvaraḥ |
samāhūyābravīt putra ! gādha kācit pragīyatām || 29 ||

items.text:
यतः प्रधानपुरुषौ यतश्चैतज्वराचरम् ।
कारणां सकलस्यास्य स नो विष्णुः प्रसीदतु ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
yataḥ pradhānapuruṣau yataścaitajvarācaram |
kāraṇāṃ sakalasyāsya sa no viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu || 30 ||

items.text:
दुरात्मा वध्यतामेष ननिनार्थोऽस्ति जीवता ।
खपक्षहानिकर्त्तृ त्वाद यः कुलाङ्गारतां गतः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
durātmā vadhyatāmeṣa naninārtho'sti jīvatā |
khapakṣahānikarttṛ tvāda yaḥ kulāṅgāratāṃ gataḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
इत्याज्ञप्तास्ततस्तेन प्रगृहीतमहायुधाः ।
उद्यतास्तस्य नाशाय दैत्याः शतसहस्त्रशः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
ityājñaptāstatastena pragṛhītamahāyudhāḥ |
udyatāstasya nāśāya daityāḥ śatasahastraśaḥ || 32 ||

items.text:
विष्णूः शस्त्रेषु युष्माकं मयि चासौ यथा स्थितः ।
दैतेयास्तेन सत्येन मा क्रामन्त्वायुधानि मे ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
viṣṇūḥ śastreṣu yuṣmākaṃ mayi cāsau yathā sthitaḥ |
daiteyāstena satyena mā krāmantvāyudhāni me || 33 ||

items.text:
ततस्तैः शतशो धैत्यैः सस्त्रौघैराहतोऽपि सन् ।
नावाप वेदनामल्पामभूज्व वै पुनर्नवः ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
tatastaiḥ śataśo dhaityaiḥ sastraughairāhato'pi san |
nāvāpa vedanāmalpāmabhūjva vai punarnavaḥ || 34 ||

items.text:
दुर्बुद्ध ! विनिवर्त्तस्व वैरिपक्षस्तवादतः ।
अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि मातिमूढ़मतिर्भव ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
durbuddha ! vinivarttasva vairipakṣastavādataḥ |
abhayaṃ te prayacchāmi mātimūṛhamatirbhava || 35 ||

items.text:
भयं भयानामपहारिणि स्थिते मनस्यनन्ते मम कुत्र तिष्ठति ।
यस्मिन् स्मते जन्मजरान्तकादिभयानि सर्व्वाणयपयान्ति तात ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
bhayaṃ bhayānāmapahāriṇi sthite manasyanante mama kutra tiṣṭhati |
yasmin smate janmajarāntakādibhayāni sarvvāṇayapayānti tāta || 36 ||

items.text:
भोभोः सर्पा ! दुराचारमेनमत्यन्तदुर्मतिम् ।
विषज्वालाकुलैर्व्वक्तूः सद्यो नयत संक्षयम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
bhobhoḥ sarpā ! durācāramenamatyantadurmatim |
viṣajvālākulairvvaktūḥ sadyo nayata saṃkṣayam || 37 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्तास्तेन ते सर्पाः कुहकास्तक्षकान्धकाः ।
अदशन्त समस्तेषु गात्रेष्वतिविषोल्वणाः ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktāstena te sarpāḥ kuhakāstakṣakāndhakāḥ |
adaśanta samasteṣu gātreṣvativiṣolvaṇāḥ || 38 ||

items.text:
स त्वासक्तमतिः कृष्णो दश्यमानो महोरगैः ।
न विवेदात्मनो गात्रं तत्स्मृत्याह्लादसंस्थितः ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
sa tvāsaktamatiḥ kṛṣṇo daśyamāno mahoragaiḥ |
na vivedātmano gātraṃ tatsmṛtyāhlādasaṃsthitaḥ || 39 ||

items.text:
दंष्ट्रा विशीर्णा मणयः स्फुटन्ति फणेषु तापो हृदयेषु कम्पः ।
नास्य त्वचः स्वल्पमपीह भिन्न प्रशाधि दैत्येश्वर कार्य्यमन्यत् ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
daṃṣṭrā viśīrṇā maṇayaḥ sphuṭanti phaṇeṣu tāpo hṛdayeṣu kampaḥ |
nāsya tvacaḥ svalpamapīha bhinna praśādhi daityeśvara kāryyamanyat || 40 ||

items.text:
हे दिग्गजाः ! सङ्कटदन्तमिशाव ! ध्नतैनमस्मद्रिपुपक्षभिन्नम् ।
तज्जा विनाशाय भवन्ति तस्य यथारणोः प्रज्वलितो हुताशाः ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
he diggajāḥ ! saṅkaṭadantamiśāva ! dhnatainamasmadripupakṣabhinnam |
tajjā vināśāya bhavanti tasya yathāraṇoḥ prajvalito hutāśāḥ || 41 ||

items.text:
ततः स दिग्गजैर्बालो भूभृच्छिखरसन्निभैः ।
पातितो धरणीपृष्ठ विषाणैरवपीड़ितः ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa diggajairbālo bhūbhṛcchikharasannibhaiḥ |
pātito dharaṇīpṛṣṭha viṣāṇairavapīṛitaḥ || 42 ||

items.text:
स्मरतस्तस्य गोविन्दमिभदन्ताः सहस्त्रशः ।
शीर्णा वक्षःस्थलं प्राप्य स प्राह पितरं ततः ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
smaratastasya govindamibhadantāḥ sahastraśaḥ |
śīrṇā vakṣaḥsthalaṃ prāpya sa prāha pitaraṃ tataḥ || 43 ||

items.text:
दन्ता गजानां कुलिशाग्रनिष्ठुराः शीर्णा यदेते न बलं ममैतत् ।
महाविपत्पापविनाशनोऽयं जनार्दनानुस्मरणानुभावः ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
dantā gajānāṃ kuliśāgraniṣṭhurāḥ śīrṇā yadete na balaṃ mamaitat |
mahāvipatpāpavināśano'yaṃ janārdanānusmaraṇānubhāvaḥ || 44 ||

items.text:
ज्वाल्यतामसुरा ! वह्निरपसर्पत दिग्गजाः ।
वायो समेधयाग्निं त्वं दह्मतामेष पापकृत्
महाकाष्ठच्छन्नमसुरेन्द्रसुतं ततः ।
प्रज्वाल्य दानवा वह्नि ददहुः खामिनोदिताः ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
jvālyatāmasurā ! vahnirapasarpata diggajāḥ |
vāyo samedhayāgniṃ tvaṃ dahmatāmeṣa pāpakṛt
mahākāṣṭhacchannamasurendrasutaṃ tataḥ |
prajvālya dānavā vahni dadahuḥ khāminoditāḥ || 46 ||

items.text:
तातैष वह्निः पवनेरितोऽपि न मां दहत्यत्र समन्ततोऽहम् ।
पश्यामि पह्मास्तरणास्तृतानि शीतानि सर्व्वाणि दिशां मुखानि ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
tātaiṣa vahniḥ pavanerito'pi na māṃ dahatyatra samantato'ham |
paśyāmi pahmāstaraṇāstṛtāni śītāni sarvvāṇi diśāṃ mukhāni || 47 ||

items.text:
अथ दैत्येश्वरं प्रोचुर्भार्गवस्यात्मजाद्रिजाः ।
पुरोहिता महात्मानः साचम्ना संस्तूय वाग्मिनः ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
atha daityeśvaraṃ procurbhārgavasyātmajādrijāḥ |
purohitā mahātmānaḥ sācamnā saṃstūya vāgminaḥ || 48 ||

items.text:
राजन् ! नियम्यतां कोपो बालेऽत्र तनयेऽनुजे ।
कोपो देवनिकायेषु यत्र ते सफलो यतः ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
rājan ! niyamyatāṃ kopo bāle'tra tanaye'nuje |
kopo devanikāyeṣu yatra te saphalo yataḥ || 49 ||

items.text: तथा तथैनं बालं ते शासितारो भविष्यति ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr: tathā tathainaṃ bālaṃ te śāsitāro bhaviṣyati || 50 ||

items.text:
बालत्वं सर्व्वदोषाणां दैत्यराजास्पदं यतः ।
ततोऽत्र कोपमत्यर्थं योक्तुमर्हसि नार्भके ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
bālatvaṃ sarvvadoṣāṇāṃ daityarājāspadaṃ yataḥ |
tato'tra kopamatyarthaṃ yoktumarhasi nārbhake || 51 ||

items.text:
न त्यक्ष्यति हरेः पक्षमस्माकं वचनाद् यदि ।
ततः कृत्यां वधायास्य करिष्यामो निवर्त्तिनीम् ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
na tyakṣyati hareḥ pakṣamasmākaṃ vacanād yadi |
tataḥ kṛtyāṃ vadhāyāsya kariṣyāmo nivarttinīm || 52 ||

items.text:
एवमभ्यर्थितस्तैस्तु दैत्यराजः पुरोहितैः ।
दैत्यैर्निष्काशयामास पुत्रं पावकसञ्चयात् ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr:
evamabhyarthitastaistu daityarājaḥ purohitaiḥ |
daityairniṣkāśayāmāsa putraṃ pāvakasañcayāt || 53 ||

items.text:
तो गुरुगृहे बालः सवसन् बालदानवान् ।
अध्यापयामास मुहुरुपदेशान्तरे गुरोः ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
to gurugṛhe bālaḥ savasan bāladānavān |
adhyāpayāmāsa muhurupadeśāntare guroḥ || 54 ||

items.text:
श्वूयतां परमार्थो मे दैतेया दितिजात्मजाः ।
न चान्यथैतन्मन्तव्यं नात्र लोभादिकारणम् ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
śvūyatāṃ paramārtho me daiteyā ditijātmajāḥ |
na cānyathaitanmantavyaṃ nātra lobhādikāraṇam || 55 ||

items.text:
जन्म बाल्यं ततः सर्वो जन्तुः प्राप्नोति यौवनम् ।
अव्याहतैव भवति ततोऽनुदिवसं जरा ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
janma bālyaṃ tataḥ sarvo jantuḥ prāpnoti yauvanam |
avyāhataiva bhavati tato'nudivasaṃ jarā || 56 ||

items.text:
ततश्यच मृत्युमभ्येति जन्तुर्दैत्येश्वरात्मजाः ।
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते चैतदस्माकं भवतां तथा ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
tataśyaca mṛtyumabhyeti janturdaityeśvarātmajāḥ |
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate caitadasmākaṃ bhavatāṃ tathā || 57 ||

items.text:
मृतस्य च पुनर्जन्म भवत्येतज्व नान्यथा ।
आगमोऽयं तथा तत्र नोपादानं विनोद्भवः ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
mṛtasya ca punarjanma bhavatyetajva nānyathā |
āgamo'yaṃ tathā tatra nopādānaṃ vinodbhavaḥ || 58 ||

items.text:
गर्भवासादि यावत् तु पुनर्जन्मोपपादनम् ।
समस्तावस्थकं तावदू दुः खमेवावगम्यताम् ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
garbhavāsādi yāvat tu punarjanmopapādanam |
samastāvasthakaṃ tāvadū duḥ khamevāvagamyatām || 59 ||

items.text:
क्षुतूतृषअमोपशमं तदूच्छीताद्यु पशमं सुखम् ।
मन्यते बालबुद्धित्वादू दुः खमेव हि तत् पुनः ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
kṣutūtṛṣaamopaśamaṃ tadūcchītādyu paśamaṃ sukham |
manyate bālabuddhitvādū duḥ khameva hi tat punaḥ || 60 ||

items.text:
अत्यन्तस्तिमिताङ्गानां व्यायामेन सुखैषिणाम् ।
भ्रान्तिज्ञानावृताक्षाणां प्रहारोऽपि सूखायते ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
atyantastimitāṅgānāṃ vyāyāmena sukhaiṣiṇām |
bhrāntijñānāvṛtākṣāṇāṃ prahāro'pi sūkhāyate || 61 ||

items.text:
क शरीरमशेषाणां श्लैष्मादीनां महाचयः ।
क कान्ति-शोभा-शौरभ्य-कमनीयादयो गुणाः ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr:
ka śarīramaśeṣāṇāṃ ślaiṣmādīnāṃ mahācayaḥ |
ka kānti-śobhā-śaurabhya-kamanīyādayo guṇāḥ || 62 ||

items.text:
मांसाऽसृकूपूयविणूमूत्रस्नायुमज्जाऽस्थिसंहतौ ।
देहे चेत् प्रीतिमान् मूढ़ो नरके भवितापि सः ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr:
māṃsā'sṛkūpūyaviṇūmūtrasnāyumajjā'sthisaṃhatau |
dehe cet prītimān mūṛho narake bhavitāpi saḥ || 63 ||

items.text:
अग्नेः शीतेन तोयस्य तषा भक्तस्य च क्षुधा ।
क्रियते सुखकर्त्तृ त्वं तदू विलोमस्य चेतदरैः ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr:
agneḥ śītena toyasya taṣā bhaktasya ca kṣudhā |
kriyate sukhakarttṛ tvaṃ tadū vilomasya cetadaraiḥ || 64 ||

items.text:
करोति हे दैत्यसुता ! यावन्मात्रं परिग्रहम् ।
तावन्मात्रं, स एवास्य दुः स्वं चेतसि यच्छति ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr:
karoti he daityasutā ! yāvanmātraṃ parigraham |
tāvanmātraṃ, sa evāsya duḥ svaṃ cetasi yacchati || 65 ||

items.text:
यावतः कुरुते जन्तुः सम्बन्धान् मनसः प्रियान् ।
तावन्तोऽस्य निखन्यन्ते ह्टदये शोकशङ्गवः ॥ ६६ ॥
items.tr:
yāvataḥ kurute jantuḥ sambandhān manasaḥ priyān |
tāvanto'sya nikhanyante hṭadaye śokaśaṅgavaḥ || 66 ||

items.text:
यदू यदू गृहे तन्मनसि यत्र तत्रावतिष्ठतः ।
नाशदाहापहरणां तत्र तस्यैव तिष्ठति ॥ ६७ ॥
items.tr:
yadū yadū gṛhe tanmanasi yatra tatrāvatiṣṭhataḥ |
nāśadāhāpaharaṇāṃ tatra tasyaiva tiṣṭhati || 67 ||

items.text:
जन्मन्यत्र महदू दुःखं म्रियमाणस्य चापि तत् ।
यातनासु यमस्योग्र गर्भसंक्रमणेषु च ॥ ६८ ॥
items.tr:
janmanyatra mahadū duḥkhaṃ mriyamāṇasya cāpi tat |
yātanāsu yamasyogra garbhasaṃkramaṇeṣu ca || 68 ||

items.text:
गर्भै च सुखलेशोऽपि भवद्भिरनुमीयते ।
यदि तत् कथ्यतामेवं सर्वं दुः खमयं जगत् ॥ ६९ ॥
items.tr:
garbhai ca sukhaleśo'pi bhavadbhiranumīyate |
yadi tat kathyatāmevaṃ sarvaṃ duḥ khamayaṃ jagat || 69 ||

items.text:
तदेवमतिदुः खानामास्पदेऽत्र भवार्णावे ।
बवतां कथ्यते सत्यं विष्णुरेकः परायणम् ॥ ७० ॥
items.tr:
tadevamatiduḥ khānāmāspade'tra bhavārṇāve |
bavatāṃ kathyate satyaṃ viṣṇurekaḥ parāyaṇam || 70 ||

items.text:
मा जानीत वयं बाला देही देहेषु शाशवतः ।
जरा-यौवन-जन्माद्या धर्म्मा देहस्य नात्मनः ॥ ७१ ॥
items.tr:
mā jānīta vayaṃ bālā dehī deheṣu śāśavataḥ |
jarā-yauvana-janmādyā dharmmā dehasya nātmanaḥ || 71 ||

items.text:
बालोऽहं तावदिच्छातो यतिष्ये श्रेयसे युवा ।
युवाहं वार्द्धके प्राप्त करिष्याम्यात्मनो हितम् ॥ ७२ ॥
items.tr:
bālo'haṃ tāvadicchāto yatiṣye śreyase yuvā |
yuvāhaṃ vārddhake prāpta kariṣyāmyātmano hitam || 72 ||

items.text:
वृद्धोऽहं मम कर्म्माणि समस्तानि न गोचरे ।
किं करिष्यामि मन्दात्मा समर्थेन न यत् कृतम् ॥ ७३ ॥
items.tr:
vṛddho'haṃ mama karmmāṇi samastāni na gocare |
kiṃ kariṣyāmi mandātmā samarthena na yat kṛtam || 73 ||

items.text:
एवं दुराशायक्षिप्तमानसः पुरुषः सदा ।
श्रेयसोऽभिमुखं याति न कदाचित् पिपसितः ॥ ७४ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ durāśāyakṣiptamānasaḥ puruṣaḥ sadā |
śreyaso'bhimukhaṃ yāti na kadācit pipasitaḥ || 74 ||

items.text:
बाल्ये क्रीड़नकासक्ता यौवने विषयोन्मुखाः ।
अज्ञा नयन्त्यशत्तया च वार्द्ध कं समुपस्थितम् ॥ ७५ ॥
items.tr:
bālye krīṛanakāsaktā yauvane viṣayonmukhāḥ |
ajñā nayantyaśattayā ca vārddha kaṃ samupasthitam || 75 ||

items.text:
तस्माद् बाल्ये विवेकात्मा यतेत श्रेयस् सदा ।
बाल्य-यौवन-वृद्धाद्यर्दैहभावैरसंयुतः ॥ ७६ ॥
items.tr:
tasmād bālye vivekātmā yateta śreyas sadā |
bālya-yauvana-vṛddhādyardaihabhāvairasaṃyutaḥ || 76 ||

items.text:
तदेतदू वो मयाख्यातं यदि जानीत नानृतम् ।
तदस्मत्प्रीतये विष्णाः स्मर्य्यतां बन्धमुक्तिदः ॥ ७७ ॥
items.tr:
tadetadū vo mayākhyātaṃ yadi jānīta nānṛtam |
tadasmatprītaye viṣṇāḥ smaryyatāṃ bandhamuktidaḥ || 77 ||

items.text:
आयासः स्मरणो कोऽस्य स्मृतो यच्छति शोभनम्
पापक्षयश्च भवति स्मरतां तमपनिंशम् ॥ ७८ ॥
items.tr:
āyāsaḥ smaraṇo ko'sya smṛto yacchati śobhanam
pāpakṣayaśca bhavati smaratāṃ tamapaniṃśam || 78 ||

items.text:
सर्व्वभूतस्थिते तस्मिन् मतिर्मैत्री दिवानिशम् ।
बवतां जायतामेवं सर्वक्ल शोन् प्रहास्यथ ॥ ७९ ॥
items.tr:
sarvvabhūtasthite tasmin matirmaitrī divāniśam |
bavatāṃ jāyatāmevaṃ sarvakla śon prahāsyatha || 79 ||

items.text:
तापत्रयेणाभिहतं यदेतदखिलं जगत् ।
तदा शोच्येषु भूतेषु द्रे षं प्राज्ञः करोति कः ॥ ८० ॥
items.tr:
tāpatrayeṇābhihataṃ yadetadakhilaṃ jagat |
tadā śocyeṣu bhūteṣu dre ṣaṃ prājñaḥ karoti kaḥ || 80 ||

items.text:
अथ भद्राणि भूतानि हीनशक्तिरहं परम् ।
मुदं तथापि कुर्व्वीत् हानिर्द्रेषफलं यतः ॥ ८१ ॥
items.tr:
atha bhadrāṇi bhūtāni hīnaśaktirahaṃ param |
mudaṃ tathāpi kurvvīt hānirdreṣaphalaṃ yataḥ || 81 ||

items.text:
बद्धवैराणि भूतानि द्र षं कुर्व्वन्ति चेत् ततः ।
शोच्यान्यहोऽतिमोहेन व्याप्तानीति मनीषिणा ॥ ८२ ॥
items.tr:
baddhavairāṇi bhūtāni dra ṣaṃ kurvvanti cet tataḥ |
śocyānyaho'timohena vyāptānīti manīṣiṇā || 82 ||

items.text:
एते बिन्नदृशा दैत्या विकल्पाः कथिता मया ।
कृत्वाभ्युपगमं तत्र संक्षेपः श्वूयतां मम ॥ ८३ ॥
items.tr:
ete binnadṛśā daityā vikalpāḥ kathitā mayā |
kṛtvābhyupagamaṃ tatra saṃkṣepaḥ śvūyatāṃ mama || 83 ||

items.text:
विस्तारः सर्व्वभूतस्य विष्णोर्विश्वमिदं जगत् ।
द्रष्टव्यमात्मवत् तस्मादभेदेन विचक्षणौः ॥ ८४ ॥
items.tr:
vistāraḥ sarvvabhūtasya viṣṇorviśvamidaṃ jagat |
draṣṭavyamātmavat tasmādabhedena vicakṣaṇauḥ || 84 ||

items.text:
समुत्सृज्यासुरं भावं तस्मादे यूयं तथा वयम् ।
तथा यत्ना करिष्यामोयथाप्राप्स्याम निर्वृतिम् ॥ ८५ ॥
items.tr:
samutsṛjyāsuraṃ bhāvaṃ tasmāde yūyaṃ tathā vayam |
tathā yatnā kariṣyāmoyathāprāpsyāma nirvṛtim || 85 ||

items.text:
या नाग्निना न वार्केण नेन्दुना नैव वायुना ।
पर्ज्जन्यवरुणाभ्यां वा न सिद्धर्न च राक्षसेः ॥ ८६ ॥
items.tr:
yā nāgninā na vārkeṇa nendunā naiva vāyunā |
parjjanyavaruṇābhyāṃ vā na siddharna ca rākṣaseḥ || 86 ||

items.text:
न यक्षैर्न च दैत्येन्द्रैर्नोरगैर्न च किन्नरैः ।
न मनुष्यैर्न पशुभिर्दोषैर्नैवात्मसम्भवेः ॥ ८७ ॥
items.tr:
na yakṣairna ca daityendrairnoragairna ca kinnaraiḥ |
na manuṣyairna paśubhirdoṣairnaivātmasambhaveḥ || 87 ||

items.text:
ज्वराक्षिरोगाऽतीसारःप्लीह-गुल्मादिकैस्तथा ।
दूषेर्ष्यामतूसराद्यैर्वा रागलोभादिभिः क्षयम् ॥ ८८ ॥
items.tr:
jvarākṣirogā'tīsāraḥplīha-gulmādikaistathā |
dūṣerṣyāmatūsarādyairvā rāgalobhādibhiḥ kṣayam || 88 ||

items.text:
न चान्यैर्नीयते कैश्विन्नित्या ह्मत्यन्तनिर्म्मला ।
तामाप्नोति मलं त्यक्ता केशवे ह्टदि संस्थिते ॥ ८९ ॥
items.tr:
na cānyairnīyate kaiśvinnityā hmatyantanirmmalā |
tāmāpnoti malaṃ tyaktā keśave hṭadi saṃsthite || 89 ||

items.text:
असारससारविवर्त्तनेषु मा यात तोषं प्रसभं ब्रवीमि ।
सर्व्वत्र दैत्याः समतामुपेत समत्वमाराधनमच्युतस्य ॥ ९० ॥
items.tr:
asārasasāravivarttaneṣu mā yāta toṣaṃ prasabhaṃ bravīmi |
sarvvatra daityāḥ samatāmupeta samatvamārādhanamacyutasya || 90 ||

items.text:
तस्मिन् प्रसन्ने किमिहास्त्यलभ्यं धर्म्मर्थकामैरलमल्पकास्ते ।
समाश्वितादू ब्रह्मतरोरनन्तान्निसं शयं प्राप्स्यथ वै महत् फलम् ॥ ९१ ॥
items.tr:
tasmin prasanne kimihāstyalabhyaṃ dharmmarthakāmairalamalpakāste |
samāśvitādū brahmataroranantānnisaṃ śayaṃ prāpsyatha vai mahat phalam || 91 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Maitreya, hear the interesting story of the wise, high-souled and magnanimous Prahlāda. In the days of yore the three worlds were brought into subjection by the valiant son of Diti—Hiranyakashipu, proud of the boon conferred on him by Brahmā. That Daitya had usurped the sovereignty of Indra and exercised the functions of the sun of air, of the lord of waters, of fire and of the moon. He himself became the lord of riches and Yama; and that Asura appropriated to himself, without reserve, all that was offered in sacrifice to the celestials. O foremost of ascetics, renouncing their own region the celestials, through his fear, wandered upon the earth, disguised in mortal shapes. Having conquered the three worlds, he was inflated with the pride of the riches, and being eulogised by the Gandharvas, enjoyed all wished-for objects. Thereupon all the Siddhas, Gandharvas and Pannagas worshipped the valiant Hiranyakashipu addicted to drinking. The Siddhas stood delighted before the Daitya chief, some singing, some playing on musical instruments and others shouting out cries of victory. When the Asura delightedly quaffed the inebriating cup in his picturesque crystal palace, the nymphs danced there gracefully.

His illustrious son, by name Prahlāda, while yet a boy, residing in the dwelling of his preceptor, read such readings as are studied in early years. Once on a time the high-souled (Prahlāda) in the company of his preceptor appeared before his father the Daitya-chief while drinking. The father Hiranykasipu, raising up his son prostrate at his feet, spoke to Prahlāda of unmitigated prowess, saying,—"Repeat, boy, agreeably, the substance of what you have read during the period". Prahlāda said,—"Hear, father I will repeat the substance of what I have read. Hear attentively what occupies my thoughts. I bow to that Great Being who is without beginning, middle or end, increase or diminution: the imperishable lord of the world, the universal cause of causes". Parāçara said:—Hearing those words the lord of the Daityas, his eyes red with ire and lip swollen with indignation, looked towards the preceptor and said,—"O vile Brahmana, what is this? O vicious-minded, thou hast, in disrespect to me, taught my boy the worthless commendation of my foe". The preceptor replied,—"O sovereign of Daityas, it doth not behove thee to give way to anger; I have not taught thy son what he has uttered". Hiranyakashipu said,—"Prahlāda, my boy, by whom then you have been thus taught. Your preceptor says that he has not instructed you thus". Prahlāda replied,—"Vishnu, O father, is the instructor of the whole world and is present in our minds. Who else, but that Great Soul can teach us (any thing)?" Hiranyakashipu said,—"O thou of vile understanding, who is this Vishnu, of whom thou art speaking again and again before me the valiant lord of the world?" Prahlāda said,—"He is Vishnu, the great God, who is being meditated upon by the devout, whose glory cannot be described in words, who is all things and from whom all things proceed". Hiranyakashipu said,—"O fool, myself living, to whom else you give the title of supreme lord? Are you desirous of death that you are mentioning this again and again?" Prahlāda replied, "O father, Vishnu, who is Brahmā, is not only the creator, preserver and supreme lord of me only, but of all creatures as well as of thyself. Be propitiated; why art thou angry?" Hiranyakashipu said,—"What evil spirit has entered into the breast of this silly lad, that, he, like one possessed, gives expression to such profane words". Prahlāda said,—"That Vishnu is not only present in my mind, but he pervades the whole universe; He is omnipresent and commands me, thyself and all creatures". Hiranyakashipu said,—"Away with this wicked boy; take him again to the preceptor's house and govern him; perhaps he has been taught by some vicious-minded (men) to sing the glories of my foes". Parāçara said:—He having said this Prahlāda was again conducted to the preceptor's house by the Daityas, where always prompt to attend upon the preceptor he received instructions constantly. After a considerable time that lord of Asuras sent for Prahlāda again and said "O my boy, recite me some poetical composition". Prahlāda said—"May that Vishnu be propitiated with us, from, whom matter and soul originate and all that is mobile and immobile proceeds and who is the cause of all this creation". Hiranyakashipu said,—"Destroy this vicious-minded boy; there is no use of his life; he is a fraud to his own family since he has proved a traitor to his kin". Parāçara said—Being thus commanded by him, hundreds and thousands of Daityas, with huge weapons, addressed themselves for his destruction. Prahlāda said to the Daityas—"Since Vishnu is present in your weapons as well as in mind, your weapons shall fail to hurt me". Parāçara said—Thereupon hundreds of Daityas assailed Prahlāda with their weapons but he did not feel the least pain and his strength was ever renewed. Hiranyakashipu said—"O you of vile understanding, refrain from glorifying my enemy; I promise you immunity, be not so foolish". Prahlāda replied: "No fear can overwhelm me since that immortal remover of all dangers is present in my mind, the very recollection of whom is enough to remove all perils consequent upon birth and human infirmities". Hiranyakashipu said—"O serpents, speedily bring this vicious lad to destruction with your envenomed fangs". Parāçara said:—Being thus commanded by him, Kuhaka, Takshaka, Artdhaka and many other venomous serpents, bit him in every part of his body. But with his mind solely devoted to Krishna he remained in that pleasurable recollection; he could not feel anything although he was bitten by deadliest serpents. The serpents said to the sovereign of the Daityas—"Our fangs are broken; our jewelled crests are shattered; our hoods are burning; Our hearts are trembling; but the skin of this body is unhurt; O king of Daityas, resort to some other expedient". Hiranyakashipu said—"O Elephants of the spheres, unite your tusks and slay this deserter of his own family and the supporter of our enemy; sometimes our own descendants bring about our own destruction as the fire consumes the wood from which it proceeds". Parāçara said:—The boy was then cast down on the earth being assailed by the tusks of those elephants of the spheres as huge as mountain peaks; but he recollecting Govinda, thousands of tusks were blunted against his breast: he then spoke to his father: "The tusks of the elephants hard as adamant have been blunted. This is not on account of any strength of mine but is consequent upon my calling upon Janārddana who destroys all dangers and sins the sources of all these evils". Hiranyakashipu said:—"Away, O ye elephants of the spheres. O Asuras, light out fire; O deity of the winds, blow up the fire, and let this perpetrator of endless iniquities be destroyed therein". Parāçara said:—Thereupon commanded by their master the Dānavas piled a huge heap of wood around the son of the king of Asuras and then put fire thereto to burn him. Prahlāda said—"This fire, although blown up by the wind, doth not burn me: I behold all around me the face of the quarters, cool, and the beds of lotuses". Parāçara said:—Thereupon the twice-born ones, the sons of Bhargava, the high-minded priests skilled in speech and the reciters of Shama Veda, eulogising him, said to the sovereign of the Daityas,—"O king, subdue thy anger against this lad, thy own begotten son. Even thy ire against the celestials bore fruits. O king, we shall so bring up this boy, that he growing humble shall engage in the destruction of thy enemies. O king of daityas, since childishness is the root of all these evils, it behoveth thee to renounce thy ire against this boy. If he according to our instructions, does not abandon the cause of Hari we shall then concert infallible measures to bring about his destruction". Parāçara said Thereupon being thus solicited by the priests the king of Daityas had his son brought out from the flames by the Daityas.

Thence-forth residing in the house of the preceptor the boy Prahlāda, whenever he got an opportunity, gave lessons himself to the sons of the Dānavas. Prahlāda said,—"O sons of the descendants of Diti, hear from me the supreme truth; do not take my instruction otherwise for there is no touch of covetousness. All creatures are born first, then they attain to infancy and youth and then succeed gradually the inevitable decay; and then they meet with death, O sons of the Daitya chiefs. This myself and you all have witnessed. He who is dead is born again—this cannot be gainsaid; the sacred texts warrant it. Birth is consequent upon the virtue and vice of pristine actions. All conditions from conception to re-birth are tinged with pain. The simpleton, in his childishness, thinks that the alleviation of hunger, thirst, cold and the like is identified with pleasure; but in sooth that is pain; for exercise gives delight to those whose limbs are incapable of motion and suffering affords pleasure to those whose understanding is blinded with delusion. Where is this vile body which is a compound of phlegm and other humours and where are its beauty, grace, loveliness and other qualities? The foolish wight will take delight even in hell, who is fond of this body composed of flesh, blood, matter, ordure, urine, membrane, marrow, and bones. The agreeableness of fire is produced by cold; of water by thirst; of food by hunger; and thus all other things are rendered agreeable by their contraries. O children of Daityas, he, who will take to a wife will introduce so much of pain into his bosom. The more a man will create dear relations, the more deeply will be implanted the thorns of anxiety in his heart. He, who has got large possessions in his house, is troubled, wherever he goes, with the anxiety that they may be lost or burnt or stolen. Then there is a great pain in being born: the dying are afflicted by the tortures of Death and again by the pain of passing into the womb. Fancy, there is not the least pleasure la the embryo state; you must then admit that the world is full of miseries. Verily I speak unto you, that in this ocean of the world infested with many miseries Vishnu is your only stay. Do not consider yourselves as mere boys and therefore ignorant of it for the spirit embodied in your bodies is eternal. Birth, youth and decay are the properties of the body not of the soul. I am now a child—when I shall be young I shall exert myself for my behoof; I am yet a youth and when I shall grow old I shall work for the benefit of my soul. I am old now—all my senses have failed me and I cannot exert myself. What shall I do now, vicious-minded as I am? I did not do anything when I was capable of doing it. Thus, men, although thirsting after knowledge, having their minds distracted by vain hopes, do not attain to beatitude. The ignorant, addicted to sport in boyhood, to worldly things in youth, find, when they become incapable, that old age is come upon them. Therefore let the soul even in childhood exert itself for its welfare independent of the conditions of infancy, youth or age. This is then what I speak unto you. If you think that it is not true, do you, for my satisfaction, think of Vishnu the liberator from all bondage. What trouble is there in calling him to mind? When remembered he bestows prosperity upon people. And if you recollect Him day and night there will be an end of all sins. Let your mind be fixed on Him day and night who is present in all beings and you shall laugh at every trouble. The whole world is subject to a triple affliction. What wise man would cherish hatred against beings who are all objects of compassion? If others are crowned with prosperity and I am incapable of enjoying the same why should I be malignant against those who are more prosperous than myself? I should rather be glad for their happiness for the suppression of malice is itself a reward. Even those who cherish malice against foes are considered as objects of pity by the wise, as being overwhelmed with delusion. O Daityas, admitting the distinction between myself and all other creatures, I have described to you the various reasons for repressing hate. Hear briefly the duties of those who approach the Deity. This whole world is the manifestation of Vishnu who is identified with all beings. The wise therefore do not regard any difference between themselves and all other creatures. Let us therefore renounce the angry passions of our race and so exert ourselves that we may obtain that perfect beatitude which is beyond the power of the deities of fire, of the sun, of the moon, of wind, of Indra, of the regent of the sea, of the Siddhas of the Rākshasas, of the Daitya-chief, of the serpents, of Kinnaras, of men, or beasts or human weaknesses and which is uninterrupted by various diseases such as fever, eye-disease &c., by hatred, malice, passion or desire. The beatitude, which can not be destroyed by others which is pure and eternal, can be enjoyed by him, who fixes his mind on Kesava. Verily I speak unto you, that you shall attain no satisfaction through various revolutions of this world. O Daityas, regard all creatures with impartiality—this is the adoration of the undecaying (Vishnu). He being propitiated what cannot be attained—wealth, pleasure, virtues are things of the little significance. Do ye resort to the exhaustless tree of true wisdom and undoubtedly you shall reap precious fruits therefrom".
